Help

What happens when my Pro or MAX hours run out?

Recording never stops and your recording is kept. A transcription that needs more hours than you have left waits until you add extra hours, switch to MAX or your hours reset, and Verbi may offer to transcribe the first part that your remaining hours cover.

Free to download, with 60 minutes of transcription every month.

Last updated: November 2, 2026

What are my options?

  • Transcribe the first part: when some hours are left, Verbi can transcribe the beginning of the file that fits in them. The whole file stays saved, and you can transcribe it in full later.
  • Add extra hours: buy a pack of 5 or 15 hours. They never expire. See how extra hours work.
  • Switch to MAX if you are on Pro: MAX has twice the hours of Pro.
  • Wait: the recording is marked as waiting for hours. When your hours reset or extra hours arrive, waiting recordings are transcribed on their own, oldest first, once you open Verbi.

How will I know before it happens?

  • When you have used 80% of your plan hours and have no extra hours, Verbi may show a card once per period; a full screen appears when your hours run out.
  • Your remaining hours and the date they reset are in Settings and on the recording screen.
  • For a YouTube video that is longer than your remaining hours, Verbi tells you how many hours you have left instead of importing it.

What if my subscription has ended?

  • Extra hours you bought stay usable after your subscription ends. Once they are used, you are on the free plan and its free minutes.
  • The free plan doesn’t use plan hours. See what the free plan includes.

Frequently asked questions

Is my recording lost when my hours run out?

No. Recording keeps working and the whole file stays saved. Only the transcription waits.

Do I have to buy extra hours?

No. You can also switch to MAX or wait for your hours to reset.

Will waiting recordings start by themselves?

Yes. When your hours reset or extra hours arrive, open Verbi and waiting recordings are transcribed one after another, oldest first.
